emirates-litfest-fringe-stage-young-perf.about:
The Fringe Stage at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature showcases young performers in front of an international festival audience. Acts can be dance, drama, music, poetry, singing or other suitable forms, solo or group, lasting 3–10 minutes; performers bring their own instruments and props.

Applications (in English or Arabic) give school details, performance title, number of performers, primary/secondary category and a description of up to 150 words, optionally with a photo or video. Places are limited; schools are contacted in February and performances happen in April 2027.

Open to students aged 3–16 living in the UAE; registration runs 27 October 2026 – 14 January 2027.
highlights: Perform at a major international literature festival
Any performing art: dance, drama, music, poetry
Free to apply
emirates-litfest-fringe-stage-young-perf.eligibility: Students aged 3–16 living in the UAE; solo or groups.
how_to_apply: Prepare a 3–10 minute act
Complete the Fringe Stage form on elfdubai.org with school details and a 150-word description
Optionally attach a photo or video
Submit by 14 January 2027

expand-north-star-supernova-2026.about:
Supernova 0X is the pitch competition of Expand North Star, the startup event that runs alongside GITEX Global. The 2026 edition is on 8–10 December 2026 at Expo City Dubai, with 60 startups pitching in stage-based rounds.

Categories are by funding raised: Pre-Seed (MVP, under USD 250k), Seed (USD 250k–3M) and Series A (USD 3–15M). Winners receive USD 20,000 / 30,000 / 70,000 in equity-free cash plus mentorship, business setup, cloud credits and market-access introductions.

Only startups registered as exhibitors at Expand North Star 2026 may apply, via the Exhibitor Portal, with a deck and a 60-second English pitch video. The final deadline is 1 November 2026.
highlights: USD 135,000 in equity-free cash prizes
Categories from pre-seed to Series A
Exposure at one of the world's largest startup shows
expand-north-star-supernova-2026.eligibility: Startups exhibiting at Expand North Star 2026 with verifiable funding in the Pre-Seed, Seed or Series A band.
how_to_apply: Book a stand or pod at Expand North Star 2026
Log in to the Exhibitor Portal (Ezone)
Submit the form, pitch deck and a 60-second English video by 1 November 2026
expand-north-star-supernova-2026.costs: Exhibiting fee (stand or pod) required; no separate competition fee stated.

founder-institute-riyadh-spring-2027.about:
The Founder Institute is a global pre-seed accelerator with chapters in many cities. Its Riyadh chapter is enrolling a Spring 2027 cohort, with an application deadline of 22 March 2027.

The programme takes founders from an idea or early product through weekly sessions and assignments on customer development, business model, branding, fundraising and incorporation, with feedback from local mentors and founders. Fewer than 40% of participants graduate, which keeps the cohort serious.

Anyone can apply from idea stage upward; applicants pick their stage in the form. An enrolment fee applies (the Silicon Valley cohort lists USD 1,099–1,599; check the Riyadh chapter's fee in the application).
highlights: Structured path from idea to fundable company
Local Riyadh mentor network plus global FI alumni
Open to first-time and student founders
founder-institute-riyadh-spring-2027.eligibility: Aspiring or early-stage founders (idea to seed) able to commit around 10–20 hours a week; any background.
how_to_apply: Open fi.co/join and pick 'Riyadh Spring 2027'
Complete the application and the stage questions
Pay the enrolment fee if accepted
Submit before 22 March 2027
founder-institute-riyadh-spring-2027.costs: Enrolment fee (Silicon Valley reference: USD 1,099 early / 1,599 regular); Riyadh fee shown during application.

georgetown-qatar-need-based-grants-2027.about:
Georgetown University in Qatar, in Doha's Education City, offers the same Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (international politics, international economics, international history, culture and politics) as Georgetown's Washington campus. Admission is need-blind: ability to pay is not a factor.

Need-based grants are available to students of any nationality; most students combine grants, scholarships and self-funding. Apply Regular Decision through the GU-Q application by 15 Jan 2027 and complete the CSS Profile by the same date so your aid package is ready for August 2027. Tuition was US$71,136 in 2025-26.
highlights: Need-blind admission for all nationalities
Georgetown School of Foreign Service degree in Doha
Need-based grants via Qatar Foundation
georgetown-qatar-need-based-grants-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Need-based grants require the CSS Profile.
how_to_apply: Submit the GU-Q application by 15 Jan 2027
Complete the CSS Profile by 15 Jan 2027
Submit any additional Qatar Foundation financial aid documents requested
Decisions released 1 April 2027
georgetown-qatar-need-based-grants-2027.costs: Need-based grants toward tuition (US$71,136 in 2025-26), housing, books and fees.

gitex-youthx-unipreneur-2026.about:
GITEX YouthX Unipreneur is the youth platform of GITEX Global and Expand North Star, aimed at students, schools, universities, young founders and educators. It combines an innovation conference with a University/Youth Innovation Expo, an Emirati Innovators Expo, youth talks and competitions, a Youth Startup & Career Pitch, mentor and investor meetings and innovation tours.

The Dubai-it Challenge Youth Edition targets innovators aged 15–25, and the event advertises more than AED 700,000 in prizes and benefits across its competitions and awards.

GITEX Global 2026 runs 7–11 December 2026 (summit at Dubai World Trade Centre, expo at Expo City Dubai). Students attend by registering as visitors; universities and young founders can book pods to exhibit.
highlights: Youth startup pitches and innovation awards
Dubai-it Challenge for ages 15–25
Access to GITEX, one of the world's largest tech shows
gitex-youthx-unipreneur-2026.eligibility: Students, school and university teams, young founders (15–25 for the Dubai-it Youth Edition) and educators; any nationality.
how_to_apply: Open the YouthX page on expandnorthstar.com
Register as a visitor through GITEX ticketing (or book a pod to exhibit)
Check the YouthX page for competition entry details
Attend 7–11 December 2026 in Dubai
gitex-youthx-unipreneur-2026.costs: Visitor ticket or exhibition pod price per GITEX; prizes and benefits worth AED 700,000+.

guq-global-challengers-2027.about:
Georgetown Global Challengers is GU-Q's autumn programme for students in years 10, 11 and 12. It starts with a short online classroom (Google Classroom) and continues with a week-long in-person practicum on campus. The current theme is the practical and responsible use of AI: using AI for research, writing, creativity, problem-solving and study, while learning about its limits, ethics and digital literacy.

The online part is open to anyone; students based in Qatar who complete the modules are invited to the campus bootcamp, capped at about 50 students per cohort. The 2025 edition ran online 26-30 October with campus cohorts on 2-6 and 9-13 November; the programme is offered every October-November.

Participants receive a certificate of completion. It is free and a good first contact with a Georgetown campus.
highlights: Free certificate programme run by Georgetown
Hands-on, responsible use of AI tools
Small cohorts of about 50 students
guq-global-challengers-2027.eligibility: High school students in years 10-12. Online modules open to all; the in-person bootcamp is only for high school students in Qatar. A Gmail account is needed for Google Classroom.
how_to_apply: Watch the GU-Q high school programmes page each September
Register through the GU-Q admissions form when it opens
Complete the online modules
Attend your assigned campus bootcamp cohort

guq-pre-college-summer-program-2027.about:
The Georgetown Pre-College Summer (GPS) Program is GU-Q's flagship summer course for high school students in Qatar. For three weeks students attend full-time, co-educational, English-language classes on the Education City campus: English (critical reading, writing, presenting), Introduction to International Relations, World Geography and Global Politics, which introduces GU-Q's four majors. An optional daily SAT preparation track is taught by Princeton Review instructors, and peer tutors who are current Georgetown students run co-curricular sessions.

The programme is meant for students who want a stronger university application and a real taste of college life. The 2026 edition ran 4-23 July with an application deadline of 30 April; the 2027 edition is expected to follow the same pattern, with applications opening in spring.

It is one of the few affordable, university-run summer programmes in Doha, and it gives direct contact with GU-Q's admissions team.
highlights: Taught on the GU-Q campus in Education City
Optional SAT preparation by Princeton Review
Lunch included every day
guq-pre-college-summer-program-2027.eligibility: Qatar nationals and residents entering the last two years of secondary school. Preference for good academic standing, a GPA of 3.0/B or 80%+ and solid English.
how_to_apply: Check the GPS page in spring 2027 for the new application link
Prepare your latest school report (GPA 3.0/B or 80%+)
Submit the online application before the deadline (late April in 2026)
Pay tuition once accepted
guq-pre-college-summer-program-2027.costs: Tuition (2026): QAR 3,700 with SAT courses, or QAR 1,850 without SAT. Lunch provided daily.

guq-university-preparedness-program-onli.about:
The University Preparedness Program is a free, asynchronous online course for high school students in grades 9-12, created by undergraduate instructors at GU-Q's Office of Educational Enrichment. It runs on Google Classroom and covers skills that matter at university, such as study habits, research and writing, and personal development.

Because it is self-paced, international students can join as easily as students in Qatar. After finishing all modules and assessments you receive a certificate of completion. The 2025 edition ran 28 September-27 November; places are first come, first served and registration closes once the class is full.

It is a no-cost way to add a Georgetown-issued certificate to your profile and practise university-style work.
highlights: Completely free and online
Open to international students
Certificate of completion from GU-Q
guq-university-preparedness-program-onli.eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 from any country. English required.
how_to_apply: Check the programme page from September
Sign up through the form (first come, first served)
Join the Google Classroom you are invited to
Complete all modules and assessments to get the certificate

hbku-qbri-shadowing-days.about:
The Shadowing Days Program lets school students experience the daily life of a biomedical researcher. Participants are matched with one of QBRI's research groups across its three centres and observe lab activities, interact with scientists and learn how research is done.

It is an easy first step before applying for longer internships such as QBRI's Summer Research Program, and it helps students test their interest in medicine and life sciences. To apply, email a PDF of both sides of your QID to QBRI; all requests are subject to approval and mentor availability.
highlights: See real biomedical labs at HBKU
Short and flexible
Simple email application
hbku-qbri-shadowing-days.eligibility: School students holding a valid Qatari residence permit.
how_to_apply: Scan both sides of your QID as a PDF
Email it to qbriinfo@hbku.edu.qa asking for a shadowing day
Wait for approval and a matched research group

hbku-qbri-throughout-the-year-internship.about:
QBRI's Throughout the Year Program offers tailored research internships for school and undergraduate students, with the length agreed between the student and the mentor. Interns are matched with one of QBRI's research groups across its three centres (including diabetes, cancer and neurological disorders) based on mentor availability and their interests, and work in the lab alongside researchers.

It complements QBRI's Summer Research Program and is a strong addition to a medicine or life-sciences application. Applications are by email with the student's QID, the internship application form and a Hepatitis B negative certificate; QF students apply via the QF internships platform.
highlights: Hands-on lab experience with HBKU researchers
Flexible timing around school
Open to school and undergraduate students
hbku-qbri-throughout-the-year-internship.eligibility: School and undergraduate students holding a valid Qatari residence permit. Students studying abroad qualify only if a parent works at Qatar Foundation and they hold a Qatari residence permit.
how_to_apply: Download the internship application form from the QBRI page
Get a Hepatitis B negative certificate
Email the form and both sides of your QID (PDF) to qbriinfo@hbku.edu.qa
QF students apply through internships.qf.org.qa

hbku-qschool-quantum-summer-school-2027.about:
QSchool is the Quantum Computing Summer School of HBKU's Qatar Center for Quantum Computing (QC2), delivered with Qatar Foundation's summer camp programme Mukhayamna. Over five days students cover quantum mechanics essentials (superposition, entanglement), quantum gates and circuits, quantum algorithms, quantum teleportation and quantum key distribution, through interactive lectures and labs on simulated and real quantum platforms.

It welcomes high school students from schools across Qatar. Editions ran in 2024 and 2025 (6-11 July 2025); future editions are announced through HBKU's events calendar and QF's Mukhayamna summer camp registration.
highlights: Hands-on with real and simulated quantum computers
Taught by HBKU quantum researchers
Rare quantum course for school students
hbku-qschool-quantum-summer-school-2027.eligibility: High school students from schools in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Watch HBKU's academic events and QF Mukhayamna announcements from May
Register through the Mukhayamna summer camp registration
Attend the 5-day programme at HBKU
hbku-qschool-quantum-summer-school-2027.costs: Not stated; Mukhayamna camps may charge a fee.

hbku-tii-youth-language-courses-2027.about:
HBKU's Translation and Interpreting Institute (TII) Language Center runs youth language courses each term in Arabic (including Arabic for non-native speakers), French, Spanish, German, Italian and Mandarin Chinese, grouped by age and level. The Fall 2026 term runs 3 October-12 December 2026 (25 hours over 11 Saturdays) in Education City; new terms for 2027 open with online registration a few weeks before classes start.

Courses suit children and teenagers who want structured language learning with qualified instructors. Fees are around QAR 1,625 per 25-hour course, with discounts for siblings, multiple courses, early-bird registration and QF/HBKU families.
highlights: Six languages for children and teens
Small Saturday classes in Education City
Early-bird and sibling discounts
hbku-tii-youth-language-courses-2027.eligibility: Children and teenagers (age groups per course, e.g. 8-12) in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Read the course descriptions and choose a level
Register online at register.tii.qa when the new term opens
Pay by credit or prepaid card to confirm your place
hbku-tii-youth-language-courses-2027.costs: About QAR 1,625 per 25-hour course (Fall 2026); discounts of 10-20% available.

hub71-plus-ai-cohort-21.about:
Hub71+ AI is one of Hub71's sector programmes in Abu Dhabi. It runs for 12 months (launch, market-entry preparation and growth phases, then a fundraising showcase and public Demo Day), with Cohort 21 starting in September 2027.

Accepted startups receive AED 250,000 in flexible in-kind incentives with service providers, AED 250,000 in cash for equity via a SAFE note, and possibly a further AED 250,000 top-up. Partners for this track include AI71, Core42, AWS, Nvidia, Google for Startups, HPE, MBZUAI and 42 Abu Dhabi (with compute and pilots).

It is for pre-seed to Series A startups in this sector; at least one founder must relocate long-term and build a team in Abu Dhabi. Apply with the form and a PDF pitch deck; selection has four rounds (review, Hub71 meeting, partner pitch, final committee). The Cohort 21 deadline is February 2027, with reviews by April 2027.
highlights: Up to AED 750,000 in cash and in-kind support
Sector partners and pilot opportunities in Abu Dhabi
Open to founders from any country
hub71-plus-ai-cohort-21.eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A startups in the track's sector, any nationality; at least one founder must relocate to Abu Dhabi long-term.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page and click Apply Now
Complete every field of the application form
Upload a PDF pitch deck (problem, solution, market, traction, team, Abu Dhabi plans)
Go through team meetings, partner pitch and the final committee
hub71-plus-ai-cohort-21.costs: No fee; AED 250k in-kind + AED 250k cash for equity (SAFE), possible AED 250k top-up for more equity.

iklc-uae-kangaroo-linguistic-2027.about:
The International Kangaroo Linguistic Competition (IKLC) is part of the Kangaroo family of contests. It is a 120-minute multiple-choice test in English that measures linguistic reasoning, comprehension and interpretation, in six age categories from Grade 1 to Grade 12.

In the UAE it is organised by ThinkTanks, the national Kangaroo member. Registration runs 30 August – 3 December 2026, confirmations follow on 14 December, the contest is held at participating schools on 27 January 2027 and results come out on 27 February 2027.

The fee is AED 150 per student (school registration is free); refunds are possible until 3 December. Homeschooled students or those whose school is not hosting can register individually.
highlights: Language-reasoning contest, no memorisation
Six categories from Grade 1 to 12
Taken at your own school
iklc-uae-kangaroo-linguistic-2027.eligibility: Students in Grades 1–12 in the UAE (via school; individual entry for homeschoolers or non-hosting schools).
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register free on kangaroouae.org (homeschoolers can register individually)
School adds each student under the competition in its profile
School pays AED 150 per student by bank transfer and uploads proof
Sit the contest at school on the set date
iklc-uae-kangaroo-linguistic-2027.costs: AED 150 per student; free school registration.

ikmc-uae-kangaroo-math-2027.about:
The International Kangaroo Mathematics Contest (IKMC) is run in more than 100 countries under the Association Kangourou sans Frontières; ThinkTanks Child Skills Development is the official UAE member. Questions reward reasoning and problem solving rather than advanced syllabus content, with papers for each level from Year 1 to Year 12.

For 2027, schools register from 30 September 2026 to 12 March 2027, registrations are confirmed by 31 March, the contest takes place on 20 April 2027 at each participating school, and results are published on 20 May 2027.

Students take part through their school, so ask your maths teacher or coordinator to register. Fees are set per student by the organiser.
highlights: Taken at your own school
All levels from Year 1 to Year 12
Internationally recognised results and medals
ikmc-uae-kangaroo-math-2027.eligibility: Students in Years 1–12 at UAE schools that register for the contest.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's maths coordinator to register on kangaroouae.org by 12 March 2027
Practise with past Kangaroo papers
Sit the contest at school on 20 April 2027
Check results on 20 May 2027
ikmc-uae-kangaroo-math-2027.costs: Per-student fee set by the organiser (not listed on the page).

iksc-uae-kangaroo-science-2026.about:
The International Kangaroo Science Competition (IKSC) tests how well students reason with everyday and basic scientific ideas; there is no fixed syllabus. It is a 120-minute multiple-choice paper in five categories: Pre-Ecolier (Grades 1–2), Ecolier (3–4), Benjamin (5–6), Cadet (7–8) and Junior (9–10).

The UAE round is run by ThinkTanks. Registration is open 3 August – 2 November 2026, confirmations go out on 12 November, the contest is held at schools on 30 November 2026 and results are due 30 December 2026.

The fee is AED 150 per student; school registration is free.
highlights: Reasoning-based science contest
Five age categories
Results before the end of 2026
iksc-uae-kangaroo-science-2026.eligibility: Students in Grades 1–10 in the UAE (via school; individual entry for homeschoolers or non-hosting schools).
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register free on kangaroouae.org (homeschoolers can register individually)
School adds each student under the competition in its profile
School pays AED 150 per student by bank transfer and uploads proof
Sit the contest at school on the set date
iksc-uae-kangaroo-science-2026.costs: AED 150 per student; free school registration.

insurance-authority-insurance-hackathon-.about:
Insurance Barmajan is the Insurance Authority's hackathon within its innovation ecosystem. Teams build solutions for the Saudi insurance sector over three days (12–14 November 2026) at The Garage in Riyadh, across four tracks covering customer experience, digital services, AI and data, embedded and on-demand insurance, and insurance for major events and mass gatherings.

It is open to university students, developers and technical specialists, innovators, entrepreneurs, startups, insurtech companies and sector experts. Winners are honoured at the ingate 2026 conference (16–18 November).

Prizes total SAR 560,000: per track SAR 80,000 / 40,000 / 20,000 for first to third place, plus seats in incubation and acceleration programmes; every applicant gets access to a digital-tools perks platform. Register by 7 November 2026.
highlights: SAR 560,000 prize pool across four tracks
Winners join incubation and acceleration programmes
Open to students as well as startups
insurance-authority-insurance-hackathon-.eligibility: University students, developers, technical specialists, innovators, entrepreneurs, startups and insurtech companies; participation is in Riyadh in person.
how_to_apply: Open the hackathon page on the Insurance Authority innovation platform
Register your team or individual profile by 7 November 2026
Wait for screening and acceptance (7–10 November)
Attend the hackathon at The Garage, Riyadh, 12–14 November
insurance-authority-insurance-hackathon-.costs: Free to participate; travel to Riyadh at own cost.

jusour-sahem-student-part-time-jobs.about:
Sahem ('contribute') is run by Jusour to bring students into Qatar's labour market. University students enrolled at accredited institutions in Qatar can take part-time jobs with companies registered on the Sahem platform, under flexible training contracts approved by the Ministry of Labour. Participants receive an experience certificate when the job ends and a Sahem card with discounts, and the experience can lead to a full-time job later.

To be eligible you must be a current student at a university or higher-education institution in Qatar, aged 17 or over, with a valid Qatari ID. Employment of Qatari students and children of Qatari women counts towards companies' Qatarization quotas.
highlights: Paid part-time work while studying
Ministry of Labour-approved contracts
Experience certificate and discount card
jusour-sahem-student-part-time-jobs.eligibility: Current university students in Qatar aged 17+ with a valid Qatari ID; also people with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Open the Sahem page on jusour.qa
Register on the Sahem platform as a university student
Apply to part-time roles posted by companies
jusour-sahem-student-part-time-jobs.costs: Free; jobs are paid by employers.

kangaroo-mawhiba-math-competition-2027.about:
Kangaroo Mawhiba is the Saudi edition of the worldwide Kangaroo mathematics competition, which rewards logical thinking and problem solving rather than advanced syllabus knowledge. Mawhiba runs it remotely on an online platform; students receive login details by email and sit the exam at the time set for their grade band.

In 2026, registration ran 2 February – 7 April, a trial test was offered 8–13 April, exams took place 17–18 April by grade band (primary grades 3–6, intermediate and secondary), and results came out on 28 April. Medals are delivered through Talent Management departments of the education directorates.

It is a low-stakes, free way for Saudi school students to try a recognised international competition and a common first step towards Mawhiba's olympiad programmes.
highlights: International contest taken online
Grade bands from primary 3 to secondary 3
Free trial test before the official exam
kangaroo-mawhiba-math-competition-2027.eligibility: General-education students in Saudi Arabia from primary grade 3 to secondary grade 3.
how_to_apply: Register on the Kangaroo Mawhiba registration page when it opens (expected February 2027)
Receive login credentials by email
Take the optional trial test
Sit the online exam at your grade's time slot
kangaroo-mawhiba-math-competition-2027.costs: No fee mentioned on the official pages.

kaust-academy-energy-transition-speciali.about:
The Energy Transition Specialization is one of KAUST Academy's four university specializations. Stage 1 is self-paced Coursera prerequisites (general chemistry, materials science, mechanics, electric fields), followed by a placement test in December, two in-person lecture stages (Renewable Energy & Storage I and II) during university breaks, and an 8-week summer programme at a KAUST Academy partner institution in Saudi Arabia or abroad with on-campus accommodation.

Students advance only by passing the assessment after each stage. Those not selected for the in-person stages keep Coursera access and can earn free certificates.

It is offered on a full scholarship to Saudi nationals (or children of Saudi citizens) aged 21–30 in years 3–5 of a Saudi university, or graduated within two years in an energy-relevant field. Apply by the online form before 5 November.
highlights: Full scholarship including summer programme accommodation
Hands-on renewable energy and storage curriculum from KAUST
Free Coursera certificates for all admitted to stage 1
kaust-academy-energy-transition-speciali.eligibility: Saudi nationals or children of Saudi citizens, aged 21–30, in the 3rd–5th year at a Saudi university or graduated within the last two years in an energy-relevant field.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page on academy.kaust.edu.sa
Submit the 2026–2027 application form before 5 November

kaust-academy-energy-transition-speciali.costs: Full scholarship: no tuition, Coursera access included, summer accommodation provided.

kaust-academy-women-in-stem-2027.about:
Women in STEM is a KAUST Academy programme that prepares Saudi women for graduate study and STEM careers. Over 15 months it combines in-person periods at KAUST with online learning aligned to the Saudi academic calendar, covering STEM training, standardised-test preparation, soft skills and academic mentorship.

It is open to female Saudi seniors and fresh graduates with a bachelor's in a STEM field. There is no minimum GPA and no TOEFL/IELTS requirement; admission is by a two-part admissions test (STEM and English, one hour each) and a personal interview.

The programme is free, including accommodation and meals during in-person periods. The last application window was 4–15 May; watch the page for the 2027 window.
highlights: Fully funded, including accommodation and meals at KAUST
No GPA or English test minimum
Prepares for graduate admissions and STEM careers
kaust-academy-women-in-stem-2027.eligibility: Saudi women in their final undergraduate year or fresh graduates with a STEM bachelor's degree.
how_to_apply: Watch the Women in STEM page for the May 2027 window
Submit the online application form
Take the STEM and English admissions test
Attend the personal interview
kaust-academy-women-in-stem-2027.costs: Free; accommodation and meals covered during in-person periods.

kaust-saudi-research-science-institute-2.about:
The Saudi Research Science Institute (SRSI) brings high-achieving high-school students to KAUST each summer for six weeks of real STEM research. Participants are placed in KAUST faculty labs, supported by mentors, and also take coursework and enrichment activities, finishing with research presentations.

It is only for Saudi national students in grade 11. The application covers biography, academic history and essays on motivation, research interests and extracurriculars, plus two recommendation letters (in English) from maths or science teachers, a 200 SAR non-refundable application fee and an online interview for eligible candidates.

In the 2026 cycle the deadline was 15 January; the 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern, so prepare essays and recommenders in November–December.
highlights: Six weeks of real research in KAUST labs
Mentored by KAUST faculty and researchers
One of the most selective pre-university STEM programmes in Saudi Arabia
kaust-saudi-research-science-institute-2.eligibility: Saudi national students in grade 11 with strong maths and science records.
how_to_apply: Read the SRSI page and application process on academy.kaust.edu.sa
Create an account on the KAUST portal and complete the online application
Ask two maths/science teachers to submit English recommendation letters
Pay the 200 SAR application fee
Attend the online interview if shortlisted
kaust-saudi-research-science-institute-2.costs: 200 SAR non-refundable application fee; programme cost coverage not stated on the page (historically residential at KAUST).

khalifa-university-undergraduate-scholar.about:
Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi is the UAE's top-ranked research university for engineering, computing and science. International (non-UAE) undergraduates are considered for a tiered scholarship: Tier I full tuition and textbooks, Tier II 75% tuition, Tier III 50%, Tier IV 25% (all with textbooks) and Tier V textbooks only.

There is no separate scholarship application: eligibility is assessed during admission and places are limited, so meeting minimum criteria does not guarantee an award. Fall 2027 applications open on the Khalifa University applicant portal; check the undergraduate admissions requirements (school grades, English test and maths/physics or SAT requirements) before applying.
highlights: Up to full tuition plus textbooks
Assessed automatically at admission
Top UAE engineering and science university
khalifa-university-undergraduate-scholar.eligibility: International (non-UAE) applicants admitted to full-time bachelor's programmes. Selection by academic merit; places limited.
how_to_apply: Check undergraduate admission requirements on ku.ac.ae
Apply on ugapply.ku.ac.ae when the Fall 2027 cycle opens
Submit transcripts, English test and required test scores
Scholarship tier is communicated with admission
khalifa-university-undergraduate-scholar.costs: Tier I: 100% tuition + textbooks; Tier II: 75%; Tier III: 50%; Tier IV: 25%; Tier V: textbooks only. Housing and living costs are separate.

king-saud-university-external-scholarshi.about:
King Saud University, Saudi Arabia's oldest and largest university, admits international students through external scholarships at three levels: Arabic-language diplomas (including the intensive diploma for non-Arabic speakers), bachelor's degrees, and postgraduate studies.

For bachelor's external scholarships, applicants must hold a recognised high-school diploma obtained within the last five years, a valid SAT score of at least 1010 (1200 for medicine), be aged 17–25, have home-government approval where required, not hold another Saudi scholarship, and pass a medical exam (plus interview/tests for medicine, dentistry and architecture). Programmes on the scholarship list include electrical, chemical, industrial, civil, mechanical and petroleum engineering, computer science and software engineering, mathematics, actuarial science, chemistry, agriculture, economics and business. KSU's benefits page lists a monthly allowance of SAR 1,000 (science programmes) or SAR 850 (other programmes) for bachelor's external scholars (SAR 900 for postgraduates), university housing, discounted meals, a two-month settling-in allowance on arrival and a three-month graduation allowance for shipping books, on top of free tuition.
highlights: Free bachelor's at Saudi Arabia's largest university
SAT ≥ 1010 route open to all nationalities
Engineering, computing, science and business programmes
king-saud-university-external-scholarshi.eligibility: International applicants living outside Saudi Arabia, aged 17–25, with a recognised secondary diploma from the last five years, SAT ≥ 1010 (≥1200 for medicine), attested documents, medical fitness and no other Saudi scholarship.
how_to_apply: Take the SAT and obtain a score of at least 1010.
Have your secondary certificates attested.
Apply online via KSU's External Scholarships portal (linked from the International Students Department page) when the window opens.
Attend interviews/tests if your programme requires them; accept the offer.
king-saud-university-external-scholarshi.costs: Free tuition; monthly allowance SAR 1,000 (sciences) / SAR 850 (other fields); university housing; discounted meals; 2-month arrival allowance; 3-month graduation allowance.

kuwait-university-outstanding-non-kuwait.about:
Kuwait University's admissions rules list several categories of applicants. Under the Outstanding Students' Scholarship, the university allocates 15 seats each year to outstanding non-Kuwaiti graduates of Kuwait's unified (government) secondary system. It also offers a number of cultural scholarships to various countries or official entities under agreements with the State of Kuwait.

GCC nationals who completed all years of secondary school in Kuwaiti high schools can apply alongside Kuwaiti students for seats in all faculties, and a separate category of 100 seats exists for stateless residents and children of non-Kuwaiti fathers. Applications are submitted online through the KU admission portal.
highlights: 15 scholarship seats for top non-Kuwaiti school graduates
Cultural scholarships for partner countries
GCC nationals schooled in Kuwait compete equally
kuwait-university-outstanding-non-kuwait.eligibility: Outstanding non-Kuwaiti graduates of Kuwait's unified secondary system (scholarship seats); citizens of partner countries via official cultural scholarship nominations; GCC nationals who completed secondary school in Kuwait (regular admission).
how_to_apply: Check Kuwait University's 'How to apply' page for your applicant category.
Apply online during the summer admission window with your secondary certificate.
For cultural scholarships, contact your Ministry of Education or Kuwait's embassy.
Contact the KU scholarships office for specifics.
kuwait-university-outstanding-non-kuwait.costs: Scholarship seats cover tuition at Kuwait University; cultural scholarships per agreement.

m7-maker-space-and-masterclasses.about:
M7 is Qatar Museums' creative hub in Msheireb Downtown Doha for fashion, design and technology. Its Maker Space, part of the Learning Space, gives designers and creatives access to industrial and home sewing machines, overlockers, mannequins, embroidery and beading tools, a silkscreen set-up and Plasticpreneur plastic grinder, injection-moulding and extruder machines. It can be booked daily or taken over for a period through a proposal.

The M7 Masterclass Series offers multi-day, skill-based programmes led by globally recognised industry figures (for example jewellery design with The Design Studio by Azza Fahmy). Upcoming masterclasses are posted on M7's calendar.
highlights: Free-to-book maker equipment for creative projects
Masterclasses with leading designers
In the heart of Msheireb, Doha
m7-maker-space-and-masterclasses.eligibility: Designers and creatives in Qatar, including art and design students.
how_to_apply: Email tlsm7@m7.org.qa to book the Maker Space or propose a takeover
Check the M7 calendar for masterclasses
Register for the masterclass you want
m7-maker-space-and-masterclasses.costs: Maker Space booking on request; masterclass fees vary.

mada-coding-camp-2027.about:
Mada Academy's Coding Camp empowers children and youth with disabilities by teaching coding fundamentals, robotics, STEAM activities, artificial intelligence and creative problem-solving in an accessible environment. A separate camp for students with visual disabilities uses accessible tools such as Code Jumper and LEGO Braille Bricks to build computational thinking.

The 2026 edition ran in separate sessions for boys (27-29 July) and girls (3-5 August). The camp is expected again in summer 2027; registration opens on Mada's website.
highlights: Fully accessible coding and robotics
Special track with LEGO Braille Bricks
Separate sessions for boys and girls
mada-coding-camp-2027.eligibility: Children and youth with disabilities aged 10-18 in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Watch mada.org.qa for the 2027 camp announcement
Register through the camp page
Choose the right track (general or visual disabilities)

mada-innovation-award-2027.about:
The Mada Innovation Award is part of the Mada Innovation Program, which encourages innovators to create Arabic assistive-technology (AT) and ICT-accessibility solutions for persons with disabilities. Applicants choose a stream: Direct Grant (a proven AT concept to develop for the local and Arab market) or Localization (adapting an existing accessible product for Arabic users). Recent categories include a Grand Impact Grant and a Scaling Innovation Grant of QAR 120,000 each, with a strong focus on AI and Arabic language.

Shortlisted innovators receive mentoring from Mada's team. The site states that the 2027 award 'will open soon'. University student teams, startups and researchers with an accessibility idea are a good fit.
highlights: Grants up to QAR 120,000
Mentoring for shortlisted teams
Focus on AI and Arabic accessibility
mada-innovation-award-2027.eligibility: Innovators, startups and organisations (including student teams) with assistive-technology or accessibility solutions for the Arab region.
how_to_apply: Watch award.mada.org.qa for the 2027 opening
Choose the Direct Grant or Localization stream
Submit your application online
Track your application via the portal
mada-innovation-award-2027.costs: Free to apply; winners receive grant funding.

mada-innovation-club.about:
The Mada Innovation Club was launched to encourage creators with disabilities and the elderly to develop innovations that support ICT accessibility. In line with the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, it builds members' capabilities in innovation, science, technology, engineering, mathematics, robotics and programming as a step towards employment, and supports entrepreneurship.

Members can use Mada's FabLab and MadaLAB, join events on the Mada Innovation Program calendar and connect with the wider Mada innovation community. Joining is through an online form.
highlights: STEM, robotics and coding for creators with disabilities
Access to Mada FabLab
Path to Mada's innovation grants
mada-innovation-club.eligibility: Persons with disabilities (including young people) and older people in Qatar interested in innovation and technology.
how_to_apply: Open the Mada Innovation Club page
Click "Join Mada Innovation Club" and complete the form
Take part in club workshops and events

manormun-vi-2027.about:
MANORMUN is the student-run MUN of Manor Hall International School in Al Ain. The sixth edition takes place on Saturday 29 May 2027. Committees include the General Assembly, Human Rights Council, FIFA, the International Criminal Court and International Court of Justice, plus a press corps.

It is aimed at secondary-school students in Al Ain and the wider UAE, with handbooks, templates and a schedule published on the official site.

A short, beginner-friendly conference that is easy to fit into the school year.
highlights: One-day format, beginner-friendly
ICJ, ICC, FIFA and press corps
Handbooks and templates online
manormun-vi-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students in the UAE, registering via their school or individually. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Visit manormun.manorhallschool.com
Read the committees and handbooks
Register through the Registration page when the form is live
Attend on 29 May 2027
manormun-vi-2027.costs: Delegate fee to be confirmed on the registration page.

mawhiba-academic-enrichment-program-2027.about:
The Mawhiba Academic Enrichment Program is a summer programme that builds scientific knowledge, practical skills and personal skills, preparing students for Mawhiba's advanced local and international programmes. The 2026 edition ran in July for three weeks: an in-person commuter format (15 days, ~60 hours) at host organisations in several cities, or an online format (45 hours) on Mawhiba's e-learning platform.

Tracks cover medical/biological/chemical sciences, physical/earth/space sciences, engineering and architecture, and computer science/applied maths/economics, with activities, projects and a closing showcase. A certificate requires 80% attendance.

It is open to students in the National Program for Gifted Identification in grades 3–11 who meet the MMCAT thresholds (1355–1400 depending on level). Saudi students and children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis can make up to 10% of places. 2026 fees ranged from 460 to 2,300 SAR.
highlights: In-person in several cities or fully online
Four science and engineering tracks
Gateway to Mawhiba's advanced and international programmes
mawhiba-academic-enrichment-program-2027.eligibility: Grades 3–11 in the National Program for Gifted Identification with the required MMCAT score; Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers (non-Saudis up to 10%).
how_to_apply: Take the Mawhiba MMCAT gifted identification test
Log in to the Enrichment Program Registration Portal when it opens
Choose in-person (city) or online and complete the form
Accept the terms and pay the fee to confirm
mawhiba-academic-enrichment-program-2027.costs: 2026 fees incl. VAT: 1,380–2,300 SAR in person; 460–575 SAR online; sponsored places may reduce fees.

mawhiba-after-school-enrichment-program-.about:
The After-School Enrichment Program continues Mawhiba's summer enrichment during the school year. It is fully online and open to boys and girls across Saudi Arabia (separate classes), with 12 units: seven for grades 7–9 and five for grades 10–11, mostly in Arabic and some bilingual, plus practical activities and projects.

The 2026 cohort ran 19 January – 4 March 2026 (Monday–Wednesday, two hours a day, 42 hours) after a December pre-test; the 2027 cohort is expected to follow the same calendar, with registration around November–December 2026.

It is for students in the National Program for Gifted Identification with the required MMCAT score; Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers (non-Saudis up to 10%). 2026 fees were about 368 SAR (grades 7–9) and 483 SAR (grades 10–11), with partial waivers for eligible families.
highlights: Fully online, nationwide
12 science and engineering units
Partial fee waivers available
mawhiba-after-school-enrichment-program-.eligibility: Grades 7–11 in the National Program for Gifted Identification with the required MMCAT score; Saudi or Saudi-mother children (non-Saudis up to 10%).

Open the After-School Enrichment Program tab when registration opens
Confirm your profile and complete the form
Pay the fee to confirm
mawhiba-after-school-enrichment-program-.costs: 2026: ~368 SAR (grades 7–9), ~483 SAR (grades 10–11); waivers for eligible families.

mawhiba-international-olympiad-program-2.about:
The Mawhiba International Olympiad Program prepares Saudi students for international science olympiads (IMO, IPhO, IChO, IBO, IOI, IJSO, IOAA). Students nominated from the National Gifted Olympiad (Scientific Track) progress through a First Elite Camp, a Second Elite Camp held each November, further camps and an intensive training phase of 30–60 days at KAUST, coordinated with the Ministry of Education.

Each camp lasts about two weeks and ends with an exam; only students who pass continue. Attendance of at least 80% is required for a certificate.

It is for Saudi nationals in grades 8–12. The way in is to register for the National Gifted Olympiad and pass its qualification stages.
highlights: Path to representing Saudi Arabia at IMO, IPhO, IChO, IBO, IOI and more
Intensive training phase at KAUST
Seven disciplines including astronomy and informatics
mawhiba-international-olympiad-program-2.eligibility: Saudi nationals in grades 8–12 nominated through the National Gifted Olympiad (Scientific Track).
how_to_apply: Register for the National Gifted Olympiad (Scientific Track) on mawhiba.sa
Pass all qualification stages
Accept nomination to the elite camps
Pass each camp exam to continue to intensive training
mawhiba-international-olympiad-program-2.costs: No fees stated; camps are run by Mawhiba with the Ministry of Education.

mawhiba-research-enrichment-program-2027.about:
The Mawhiba Research Enrichment Program introduces high-potential students to real scientific research. Working with specialists at partner universities, hospitals and research institutes, students do hands-on lab work and learn research methods and ethics; full-time, part-time and (where available) online formats are offered.

The 2026 session ran 5–30 July 2026 with registration from 2 February to 18 May 2026, so the 2027 cycle is expected on a similar timeline.

Applicants must be Level 3 (grades 9–11) in the National Program for Gifted Identification with an MMCAT score of 1400+ (plus an English score if the MMCAT was taken in Arabic). Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis up to 10%. 2026 fees were 3,000 SAR full-time and 1,750 SAR part-time, with discounts and waivers for some groups.
highlights: Real lab research with university and hospital scientists
Strong preparation for ISEF and research olympiads
Discounts and fee waivers for eligible families
mawhiba-research-enrichment-program-2027.eligibility: Grades 9–11, Level 3 of the National Program for Gifted Identification, MMCAT 1400+; Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers (non-Saudis up to 10%).
how_to_apply: Achieve the required MMCAT score
Apply through the Research Enrichment registration service when it opens (expected February 2027)
Wait for the nomination notice
Pay the fee to confirm your place
mawhiba-research-enrichment-program-2027.costs: 2026: 3,000 SAR full-time, 1,750 SAR part-time (VAT excluded); 15% discount for MMCAT 1550+; waivers for eligible groups.

mawhiba-science-week-program-2027.about:
Mawhiba's Science Week offers two five-day tracks held with partner schools in Riyadh and Jeddah, 4–7 pm Sunday to Thursday (15 hours per track). The scientific track covers engineering sciences; computer science and applied maths; physics, earth and space sciences; and medical, biological and chemical sciences. The skills track covers logical thinking, critical thinking, complex problem-solving, self-confidence and digital safety.

It is for students from primary grade 4 to intermediate grade 3 in the National Program for Gifted Identification with MMCAT scores of 1370+ (grades 4–6) or 1355+ (intermediate). The 2026 edition ran in April; 2027 is expected in a similar window.

The fee is 345 SAR per track (172.5 SAR with partial exemption).
highlights: Short, in-person science week for younger gifted students
Scientific and skills tracks
Low fee with waivers
mawhiba-science-week-program-2027.eligibility: Primary grade 4 to intermediate grade 3, enrolled in the gifted identification programme with required MMCAT; Saudi or Saudi-mother children (non-Saudis up to 10%).
how_to_apply: Check the programme page for the 2027 window
Register via Mawhiba's Enrichment Programs portal
Accept the terms and pay the fee
mawhiba-science-week-program-2027.costs: 345 SAR per track incl. VAT (172.5 SAR with partial exemption).

mawhiba-skills-enrichment-program-2027.about:
The Mawhiba Skills Enrichment Program develops personal skills in two tracks: oratory and public speaking, and artificial intelligence and machine learning (delivered with the Saudi Digital Academy). Sessions run on Saturdays, 9 am–1 pm, for seven weeks (28 hours), from 20 March to 1 May 2027.

In-person groups meet at partner schools in Riyadh, Jeddah, Dhahran and Buraydah; students elsewhere join remotely. It is for middle and high-school students in the National Program for Gifted Identification with MMCAT scores of 1355+ (middle) or 1400+ (high school); Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers, with non-Saudis up to 10%.

Registration normally opens in November and runs to February. Fees (incl. VAT) were 575/345 SAR (public speaking, in person/remote) and 230/115 SAR (AI & ML).
highlights: AI & ML track with the Saudi Digital Academy
In person in four cities or online
Low fees, with partial waivers
mawhiba-skills-enrichment-program-2027.eligibility: Middle and high-school students in Mawhiba's gifted identification programme with the required MMCAT score; Saudi or Saudi-mother children (non-Saudis up to 10%).
how_to_apply: Log in to mawhiba.sa and open the Skills Enrichment service
Choose track and in-person city or remote
Complete the form and accept the terms
Pay the fee before the February close
mawhiba-skills-enrichment-program-2027.costs: Public speaking 575 SAR in person / 345 SAR remote; AI & ML 230 / 115 SAR (VAT incl.).

mawhiba-tech-generation-program-2026.about:
Tech Generation is a Mawhiba programme that develops technology skills among gifted students identified through the National Program for Gifted Identification. Nominated students choose a course and attend either in person or remotely.

It is open to Saudi students from the third year of intermediate school to the third year of secondary school who hold the required score on the Mawhiba Multiple Mental Abilities Test (MMCAT). Registration is done through the Mawhiba services system.

The guardian contribution is 115 SAR for in-person and 57.5 SAR for remote attendance (VAT included). Registration ends on 10 November 2026.
highlights: Technology courses for nominated gifted students
In-person or remote options
Very low cost (57.5–115 SAR)
mawhiba-tech-generation-program-2026.eligibility: Saudi students in the National Program for Gifted Identification, from intermediate year 3 to secondary year 3, with the required MMCAT score.
how_to_apply: Log in to the Mawhiba website
Confirm your profile information
Open the Tech Generation service and choose the programme and course
Accept the terms and pay the contribution by 10 November 2026
mawhiba-tech-generation-program-2026.costs: Guardian contribution 115 SAR (in person) or 57.5 SAR (remote), VAT included.

mawhiba-universal-enrichment-program-202.about:
The Mawhiba Universal Enrichment Program is an in-person summer programme offering intensive enrichment courses in science and technical fields, delivered by international experts in gifted education. Students also build academic and personal skills through activities and group trips.

The programme runs at King Saud University for three weeks in July; boys attend a residential programme on campus and girls a day programme. The last published edition cost about 4,025 SAR (boys, residential) and 2,530 SAR (girls, day).

Applicants must be Level 3 (grades 9–11) in the National Program for Gifted Identification with an MMCAT score of 1400+ and, if the test was taken in Arabic, a minimum English score (e.g. IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 53). Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers are eligible; non-Saudis up to 10%.
highlights: Courses taught in English by international experts
Residential option at King Saud University
Trips and personal-skills activities
mawhiba-universal-enrichment-program-202.eligibility: Grades 9–11, Level 3 of the National Program for Gifted Identification, MMCAT 1400+, plus English score if MMCAT taken in Arabic; Saudi nationals or children of Saudi mothers (non-Saudis up to 10%).
how_to_apply: Register in the National Program for Gifted Identification and reach the score
Log in to the Mawhiba website and open the Universal Enrichment Program tab
Confirm your profile and complete the participation form
Accept the guidelines and pay the fee
mawhiba-universal-enrichment-program-202.costs: Last published fees: ~4,025 SAR (boys, residential) and ~2,530 SAR (girls, day), VAT included.

mdx-dubai-winter-camp-2026.about:
Middlesex University Dubai runs a Winter Camp for school students during the December break, 14–18 December 2026, 9 am–6 pm daily. Mornings are specialist workshops and discovery sessions in subjects such as business, computer engineering, fashion, media and law, plus academic-skills workshops and a campus tour; afternoons are team-building games and activities, with optional excursions.

It is a low-pressure way to sample university subjects and campus life in Dubai before choosing a degree. International visitors can contact the camp team for arrangements.

The fee is AED 1,700 for the week (excursions extra). Register via the apply option on the camp page or by contacting the team.
highlights: Taster workshops across six subject areas
Campus experience at a UK university branch
Short winter-break format
mdx-dubai-winter-camp-2026.eligibility: School students (age range not specified); international visitors should contact the team.
how_to_apply: Open the Winter Camp page on mdx.ac.ae
Use the apply option or contact the team by WhatsApp/email
Pay the AED 1,700 fee
Attend 14–18 December 2026
mdx-dubai-winter-camp-2026.costs: AED 1,700 per camp; optional excursions extra.

misk-fellowship-2027.about:
The Misk Fellowship is a hybrid, English-language leadership accelerator that aims to discover, develop and connect high-potential Saudi youth leaders. Over six months fellows complete a leadership bootcamp, compete on UN SDG-related challenges facing Saudi Arabia, receive one-to-one coaching and attend leadership masterclasses and professional development modules, with activities both in Saudi Arabia and abroad.

It is open to Saudi bachelor's, master's and PhD students (any major, no age limit) who are enrolled at or admitted to a top international university, show leadership potential and commit to all mandatory events and to community service.

The programme is free; Misk covers flights, accommodation and training for international activities. Selection is by Misk Hub application, an online psychometric test and a virtual interview.
highlights: Free, with international activities fully covered
One-to-one leadership coaching
Strong Misk alumni network
misk-fellowship-2027.eligibility: Saudi nationals studying (or admitted) at a top international university, bachelor's to PhD, any major.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on Misk Hub
Select Misk Fellowship and click Notify Me / Apply when open
Complete the online psychometric test
Attend a virtual one-on-one interview
misk-fellowship-2027.costs: Free; flights, accommodation and training for international activities covered. Not a scholarship.

misk-npo-essentials-masterclasses.about:
The Misk NPO Essentials Masterclasses are a short online series for current and aspiring non-profit leaders. Across masterclasses of 1.5–2 hours each (about four hours in total) they cover non-profit management, stakeholder management, programme design and evaluation, fundraising, social-impact measurement, digital transformation and wellbeing-economy principles, aligned with Saudi Vision 2030.

The course is self-paced, in Arabic with English subtitles, and has no prerequisites; beginners and students interested in the social sector are welcome.

Enrol through Misk Hub before 31 December 2026.
highlights: Free and self-paced
Practical non-profit and social-impact skills
Arabic with English subtitles
misk-npo-essentials-masterclasses.eligibility: Anyone interested in the non-profit sector; no prerequisites or nationality limits stated.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on Misk Hub
Open the NPO Essentials Masterclasses page
Click Enroll Now before 31 December 2026
Complete the masterclasses online

msy-al-khor-girls-centre.about:
Al Khor Girls Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 15-39, with a focus on drama and theatre, culture and leadership for young women.

Founded in 2011 in Al Khor, north of Doha, it aims to be the leading incubator for young Qatari women and their leadership in all fields. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
Workshops, clubs, trips and volunteering
A local place to build skills and friendships
msy-al-khor-girls-centre.eligibility: Young people aged 15-39 living in Qatar. Activities are mostly in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open the centre's page on the Ministry of Sports and Youth website
Contact the centre (alkhorgirls@msy.gov.qa) or visit during opening hours
Register as a member or for a specific activity
msy-al-khor-girls-centre.costs: Most activities are free or low-cost.
